messages:
Maya: Heads-up — rolled back the canary for the upstream auth-check shim. Canary triggered metric alert: dashboard p95 regressions ~15-20% on small/median panels. Rolling back while we triage. Logs + short repro below.

Sam: Saw this too, thanks for rollback. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~145ms on our synthetic panel queries (1–3 shards). Repro command I used: `ab -n 1000 -c 20 POST /api/console/query -d '{\"panel\":42,...}'` — attach trace.

Frank: Quick thoughts on tradeoffs:
- Pre-filter (auth pushed into query layer) reduces work returning rows but increases cache/key variety -> cache miss rate up.
- Post-filter (fetch then filter in console) keeps downstream caches hot, but wastes compute + network for unauthorized rows.
- The shim as implemented does a sync call per request to the auth service which amplified latency under burst.

Lia: +1 on the sync call being the smoking gun. Our role->tenant mapping endpoint is heavy (joins across membership tables). If the shim makes that call per incoming query it multiplies cost. We have a small LRU in the auth service but TTLs are short.

Dev-bot: :warning: deploy-bot rolled back canary 2376543002 -> stable at 2376543200 due to alert: console.dashboard.p95 > 130ms for 5m.

Ryan: Proposal for longer-term: define a thin auth-pushdown contract instead of doing full membership lookups inline. Two options:
1) Predicate pushdown: query layer accepts an opaque `auth_predicate_id` and uses local predicate cache. Auth service computes predicate (set of tenant IDs, or a small ACL blob) asynchronously and stores it in the predicate cache with short TTL. Query layer joins against predicate table (optimized, indexed).
2) Batch-canary RPC: the shim batches membership checks for an incoming batch of queries (same user) and returns a single authorization result.

Example minimal API (proto-ish):
```
message AuthPredicate { string id = 1; repeated string tenant_ids = 2; int64 expires_at = 3; }
service AuthService { rpc ComputePredicate(UserId) returns (AuthPredicate); }
```

Pros/cons: predicate cache reduces per-request auth RPCs (good for latency), but needs invalidation semantics when roles change. Batch RPC is simpler but requires batching coordination in the runtime.

Maya: These are good options. Short-term action items:
- Lia + Frank: instrument the shim to surface auth RPC latency and cache hit/miss rates (add metrics: auth.rpc_ms, auth.cache_hit boolean).
- Sam + Ryan: prototype a tiny predicate cache in the query layer for canary (TTL 30s) so we can measure cache hit effect without full infra changes.
- Devops: keep canary rolled back and hold new deploys to console-auth-shim until we have fixes.

Sam: I'll take the prototype. Will ping here when I have numbers. If predicate cache proves >70% hit and reduces p95 back close to baseline we'll iterate on the contract.

Frank: FYI: also watch for cache cardinality explosion — suggest we hash tenant sets and limit cached entries per user scope.

Maya: Thanks. Meeting if needed after initial numbers. @Lia @Frank can you post the auth service dashboard links once metrics are added? :thumbsup:
